m2cards.name: Net new MRR
m2cards.ok: Changes add along every axis. Q2: −19,960 + 9,775 + 42,565 = 32,380.

wrong.semi: A change adds across time too. Q2 net new is the sum: 32,380.
wrong.non: It is not a rate. Changes add: Q2 net new is 32,380.

m2cards.name: Expansion MRR
m2cards.ok: Changes add across countries and months. Q2: CH 1,990 down to GB 705, total 12,895.

wrong.semi: Expansion is a change, so it also adds across months: Q2 total 12,895.
wrong.non: It is not a rate. Countries add: Q2 total 12,895.

m2cards.name: Ending MRR
m2cards.ok: Add across segments at one moment. Never across months: 334,675 + 344,450 + 387,015 = 1,066,140 describes nothing.

wrong.additive: Added across months, three levels give 1,066,140, which describes nothing.
wrong.non: Levels do add across segments at one moment. They only fail across time.

m2cards.name: Active accounts
m2cards.ok: June: 44 + 44 + 44 = 132 across segments. Across months, 123 + 123 + 132 = 378 counts account-months; 141 distinct accounts were active in Q2.

wrong.additive: 123 + 123 + 132 = 378 counts account-months, not accounts. Distinct in Q2: 141.
wrong.non: At one moment, segment counts add: 44 + 44 + 44 = 132.

m2cards.name: Logo churn rate
m2cards.ok: Recompute from the counts: 12 of 120 = 10.0 %. Never add 10 + 10 + 10.

wrong.semi: A rate never adds, not even across segments. Recompute: 12 of 120 = 10.0 %. And 4 of 48 = 8.33 % is the wrong base.

blanks.with: Apr, May, Jun, each complete. Never add months together

rules.label: Grain in the name and the key

ddlMrr: s.data_loaded_at_utc,                            -- a fact, not an age
WHERE m.month_start <= s.complete_through_month    -- complete months only
GROUP BY m.month_start, s.complete_through_month, s.data_loaded_at_utc, s.quality_status;
-- no now(): the caller states the evaluation clock
ddlChurn: FROM bounds AS b CROSS JOIN core.load_status AS s
JOIN core.account_months AS st                    -- base: active at the end of March
JOIN core.account_months AS e ON e.account_id = st.account_id AND e.month_start = b.last_month
JOIN core.accounts AS a ON a.account_id = st.account_id
WHERE b.last_month <= s.complete_through_month;   -- complete quarters only

rows: Core is small or indexed and queries are fast enough. FOLDLINE uses views.
A view is too slow and a known lag is acceptable. The refresh time becomes data_loaded_at_utc.
Build into a new table, run the checks, then swap names in one transaction
Many readers and a strict rule that only tested data is visible.

messages.C01: Specify the MRR meaning: ending MRR, net-new MRR, or an MRR movement component.
messages.R01: Profit cannot be calculated because the approved dataset contains no cost, COGS, recognized-revenue, or approved profit definition. MRR is not a profit proxy.
messages.R02: Direct customer identifiers are outside the approved AI data surface. Use approved pseudonymous analytics keys or an authorized operational workflow.
messages.Q3: The requested period is not complete on the approved serving view.
messages.QUALITY: The serving view has not passed its required quality gate.

setups.lead: No code. Upload the approved files and paste the instructions. A Project has no database connection, so the files you upload are everything Claude can see. This is Project B in the live demo.
A repository with written guidance, a Skill and a hook. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md and loads the Skill when its description matches the question.
Claude Code queries PostgreSQL through an MCP connector that logs in as the read-only reader. The hook checks each query; the role is the lock. Add this to the Claude Code setup.

PROJECT-INSTRUCTIONS.txt.job: Tells Claude how to behave: read the data status first, ask back, refuse, and end every answer with a trace. It guides; it cannot stop Claude from reading a file you uploaded.

metric-definitions.md.job: The compiled copy of semantic/metric.yml for this reader. Loaded is not the same as used: the instructions must require the citation.

mrr_summary_monthly.csv.job: The MRR summary view as a file. In a Project there is no database, so the files you upload are the edge of what Claude can see. That upload set plays the part of the grants: upload approved views only, never the export tables “for context”.

logo_churn_by_segment_quarter.csv.job: The churn view as a file, with starting and churned accounts beside the rate. Part of the upload set that plays the part of the grants.

expansion_mrr_by_country_monthly.csv.job: The dense month-by-country grid as a file: 18 months × 8 countries = 144 rows, zeros explicit. Part of the upload set.

account_mrr_monthly.csv.job: Pseudonymous account keys only: 144 accounts × 18 months. Pseudonymous is not anonymous, so the instructions keep a row limit. Part of the upload set.

data_status_by_view.csv.job: Load time, last complete month, quality gate and thresholds for the four data views. Claude computes the age against the stated clock. Part of the upload set.

CLAUDE.md.job: Project memory for Claude Code. It guides every session in this repository. It never holds a connection string.

SKILL.md.job: Claude loads a Skill when its description matches the task. Name the trigger words; “analytics helper” never triggers, or triggers everywhere.

references/metrics.md.job: The compiled metric definitions the Skill points to. Same name and version as metric.yml, or the readers drift.

settings.json.job: Registers the hook that runs before every database tool call. It changes what Claude Code does; it does not change what the database allows.

sql_guard.py.job: A deterministic check before the query runs: one read-only SELECT on the five allowlisted views. Exit code 2 blocks the call and tells Claude why. Another client on the same login skips it: a guardrail, not a lock.

.mcp.json.job: Tells Claude Code which connector to start and which environment variable holds the connection. It names the secret; it never contains it. A connector's read-only switch is a guardrail too.
.mcp.json.dest: Copy to .mcp.json at the repository root

60_access.sql.job: The only file here that enforces. The database denies everything else with 42501, whatever the instructions say.

benchChips.label: Change read as a level
benchChips.say: Caught by G01 and Q02 in the database plane, and by value grading in the AI plane: the export tables matched 0 of 3.

benchChips.label: Retry duplicates
benchChips.say: Caught by G04 (AT 1,565, not 1,955) and Q01 (zero duplicate keys).

benchChips.label: Partial period
benchChips.say: Caught by Q03: nothing is served after complete_through_month.

benchChips.label: Read-only mode as the lock
benchChips.say: Caught by B-W01: even after BEGIN READ WRITE, the write fails with 42501.

benchChips.label: TEMP left to PUBLIC
benchChips.say: Caught by B-T01: CREATE TEMP TABLE fails with 42501.

benchChips.label: Unqualified names
benchChips.say: Caught by B-S01 (42P01 with an empty search_path) and seen in the recorded approved-lane SQL.

benchChips.label: Hidden data age
benchChips.say: Caught by F01 at a frozen 60-hour clock: answer with a warning.

benchChips.label: Definition loaded, not cited
benchChips.say: No database check can catch it. Only the AI plane's citation grade shows it: the approved-lane runs cited the definition 0 of 3.

benchChips.label: One run as a benchmark
benchChips.say: Only the run log shows it: one run each. Aim for three per case, and call each an observation.
